title: अभिहितान्वयवाद र अन्विताभिधानवाद : भाषावैज्ञानिक र शैक्षणिक सम्बन्ध {Abhihitanvaism and Anvitabhaidhanism: Linguistics and Academic Relations}
nepali: रस्तुत लेख पूर्वीय भाषिक चिन्तनमा देखापरेका अभिहितान्वयवाद र अन्विताभिधानवादको भाषाविज्ञान र भाषाशिक्षणसँग सम्बन्ध खोजी गर्ने उद्देश्यमा केन्द्रित रहेको छ । वैयाकरणहरुद्वारा स्थापित वर्ण, पद तथा वाक्यको स्वतन्त्र सत्तामाथि मीमांसक र नैयायिकहरुले मतभेद प्रकटगरेपछि अर्थबोधका सन्दर्भमा पदवादी र वाक्यवादी दृष्टिकोणका फलस्वरुप अभिहितान्वयवाद र अन्विताभिधानवाद प्रर्वतन भएको देखिन्छ । सामग्री सङ्कलनको पुस्तकालयीय कार्य अवलम्बन गरिएको यस लेखमा नेपाली र हिन्दी स्रोतका अनुसन्धानमूलक पुस्तक, शोध, स्वतन्त्र लेख, जर्नल, आदि सामग्रीको प्रयोग गरिएको छ । तथ्य वा सामग्रीको विश्लेषणका लागि वर्णनात्मक एवं विश्लेषणात्मक विधि प्रयोग गरिएको प्रस्तुत लेखमा पद द्वारा सङ्केतित अर्थलाई स्वतन्त्र सत्ता मान्ने वा वाक्यलाई अखण्डित रुपमा अर्थबोधको एकाइ मान्ने भन्ने पक्षमा मीमांसाशास्त्रमा मतभेद रहे पनि वाक्यार्थ बोधका लागि पदहरु तथा तिनका अर्थको परस्पर सम्बन्ध रहने पक्षमायी दुवै सम्प्रदायबिच सहमती देखिन्छ । भाषा विज्ञानको प्रमुख शाखा अर्थविज्ञानसँग यी दुवैको घनिष्ट सम्बन्ध रहेको देखिन्छ । अर्थ बोधका लागि वाक्यमा विन्यस्त पद नै प्रमुख हुने, पदहरुका अर्थबिचको पारस्पारिक सम्बद्धताले अर्थबोधलाई सशक्त बनाउने, एक पदीय संरचनालेपनि वाक्यको अर्थलाई सम्प्रेषित गर्न सक्ने र पदको अर्थ प्रयोगद्वारा निर्धारित हुन्छ भन्ने जस्ताविचारले भाषा शिक्षणसँग घनिष्ट सम्बन्ध राखेको देखिन्छ । यसर्थ शब्दार्थ, वाक्य निर्माण, भाषिकबोध क्षमताका साथै विद्यार्थीहरुमा वर्ण, रुप, पद, पदावली, उपवाक्य र अन्ततः वाक्यको अर्थपूर्णप्रयोगको सामथ्र्य विकास गराउने प्रयोजनमा अभिहितान्वयवाद र अन्विताभिधानवादका विचारमनन योग्य रहेको निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: The present article focuses on the objective of exploring the relationship of Abhihitanvayavada and Anvitabhidhanavada, which appeared in Eastern linguistic thought, with linguistics and language teaching. After Mimamsakas and Naiyayikas expressed disagreement over the independent existence of phonemes, words, and sentences established by grammarians, Abhihitanvayavada and Anvitabhidhanavada appear to have been initiated as a result of word-oriented and sentence-oriented perspectives in the context of meaning comprehension. In this article, in which library-based work was adopted for material collection, materials such as research books, dissertations, independent articles, and journals from Nepali and Hindi sources have been used. In the present article, which employs descriptive and analytical methods for the analysis of facts or materials, although differences of opinion exist within Mimamsa philosophy over whether to consider the meaning indicated by words as an independent entity or to regard the sentence as an indivisible unit of meaning comprehension, agreement is seen between both of these schools on the premise that words and their meanings maintain a mutual relationship for comprehending sentence meaning. Both of these are seen to have an intimate relationship with semantics, a major branch of linguistics. Ideas such as words arranged in a sentence being primary for meaning comprehension, the mutual interconnection between word meanings strengthening semantic understanding, even a single-word structure being able to convey sentence meaning, and the meaning of a word being determined by usage appear to have a close connection with language teaching. Hence, it is concluded that the ideas of Abhihitanvayavada and Anvitabhidhanavada are worthy of consideration for word meaning, sentence formation, and linguistic comprehension skills, as well as for the purpose of developing students' capacity in the meaningful use of phonemes, morphemes, words, phrases, clauses, and ultimately sentences.

informal_english: This article is all about looking into how Abhihitanvayavada and Anvitabhidhanavada, which popped up in Eastern linguistic thought, actually connect with linguistics and language teaching. After the Mimamsakas and Naiyayikas clashed with grammarians over whether sounds, words, and sentences can stand on their own two feet, Abhihitanvayavada and Anvitabhidhanavada kicked off from word-focused and sentence-focused views on making sense of meaning. Using good old library work to collect material, this article draws on stuff like research books, dissertations, standalone articles, and journals from Nepali and Hindi sources. In this article, using descriptive and analytical methods to pull apart the facts and material, even if folks in Mimamsa philosophy argue over whether a word's meaning is its own thing or if the sentence is one unbroken chunk of meaning, both camps totally agree that words and their meanings have to connect with each other to get what a sentence actually means. Both of these clearly have a proper close link with semantics, a major branch of linguistics. Ideas like words laid out in a sentence being key for catching the meaning, the mutual link between word meanings making comprehension stronger, even a single-word setup being able to get across a sentence's meaning, and word meaning being settled by usage clearly have a lekker connection with language teaching. So the conclusion is that thinking through the ideas of Abhihitanvayavada and Anvitabhidhanavada is genuinely worthwhile for word meaning, sentence construction, and language grasp, as well as for helping students build up their capacity to use sounds, forms, words, phrases, clauses, and ultimately sentences in a meaningful way.
